citation: G. Betz, Alloy sputtering, Surface Science 92, 283–309 (1980)
source_location: Fig. 13, p. 304 (PDF page 22); method in Section 3, pp. 301–302; Cu–Ni sample preparation in Section 3.2, p. 303.

conditions.target: Cu–Ni solid-solution films sputter-deposited from Cu and Ni targets on glass
conditions.temperature_note: Not specified for the Cu–Ni yield experiment in Sections 3 and 3.2.

observable: Total sputtering yield in atoms/incident ion versus bulk Cu atomic percent. Section 3 describes dividing areal atom inventory by ion fluence to the film/substrate interface (50% AES signal decrease); this is a film-integrated erosion measurement, not a resolved steady-state surface flux.
method_limit: Section 3 describes quartz microbalances for the evaporated systems. Section 3.2 states Cu–Ni films were sputter-deposited and of known composition, without detailing a separate Cu–Ni inventory calibration. Do not assign the evaporation preparation procedure to Cu–Ni.

uncertainty.note: No per-point error bars or full experimental uncertainty stated for Fig. 13. The 3% beam-current stability is one contribution, not the total yield uncertainty. CSV digitization bounds describe reading the figure only; missing experimental uncertainty must not be interpreted as zero.

columns.row_id: Stable marker identifier corresponding to the two-read record.
columns.bulk_cu_at_percent: Digitized bulk Cu atomic percent; Ni is the balance.
columns.total_yield_atoms_per_ion: Digitized measured total sputtering yield, atoms per incident Ar+ ion.
columns.cu_digitization_bound_at_percent: Estimated absolute digitization bound, not 1 sigma or experimental uncertainty.
columns.yield_digitization_bound_atoms_per_ion: Estimated absolute digitization bound, not 1 sigma or experimental uncertainty.

terms: Facts, cited; measured markers only. Original PDF, figure image, article text and fitted curve are not redistributed.
limitations: Do not combine with Ho1976 as a single matched experiment: Betz uses normal incidence and Ho about 20 degrees from normal.
The 4.8 (Cu) and 2.9 (Ni) atoms/ion quoted in the source are extrapolated fit endpoints, not additional Fig. 13 measurements.
A steady-state comparison requires a documented approximation for the film-integrated measurement.
These points provide total yield only, not new independent surface-composition data.
validation_status: Source data only; no Lindhard comparison run. Experimental uncertainty remains unresolved.
